repoLayout.packages/backend: Express API + BullMQ workers + Supabase access
repoLayout.packages/fix-engine: Validated-fix pipeline + agentic generator + CI watcher
repoLayout.packages/vector-indexer: Repo chunker + Voyage embedder + Pinecone store

flows.name: Onboarding & Integration Setup
flows.summary: Operator connects a scanner, installs the GitHub App, supplies a Claude key, picks repos, and (optionally) writes custom prompts. Each integration's credentials live in encrypted cookies on the dashboard or in the org's settings_json row in Supabase.
flows.trigger: User opens /onboarding (or /settings to add an integration later)

steps.action: Pick scanner (Aikido / Snyk) and submit API credential
Validate credential
steps.detail: Token stored as encrypted cookie; never sent to backend except as job payload

steps.action: Click 'Connect GitHub App'
Redirect to GitHub App install URL (or recover existing install)
Callback with installation_id
Save installation_id + account login on organizations.settings_json.integrations.github
Submit Claude API key
Validate key (list models)
Select repos to monitor + write custom prompts (env, conventions, testing, business)
PATCH /api/org/prompts and /api/org/settings
Persist organizations.custom_prompts_json and settings_json

outputs: organizations row populated with github installation + custom prompts
Dashboard is wired to trigger fixes and ingest scanner data
failureModes: GitHub App slug missing in env → install button errors
Multi-installation orgs not auto-recovered; user must pick install explicitly
Bad scanner credential → cookie set but later API calls 401

flows.name: Scanner Webhook Ingestion
flows.summary: Aikido and Snyk push findings via HMAC-signed webhooks. The backend verifies the signature, normalizes the payload through the scanner adapter, upserts on (org_id, scanner_source, external_id), and writes an audit-log entry.

steps.action: POST /webhooks/aikido (or /webhooks/snyk) with X-*-Signature header
verifyHmac(body, signature, secret) with timingSafeEqual
AikidoAdapter.normalizeWebhookPayload → NormalizedFinding[]
upsertFindings(orgId, findings) — dedupes on (org_id, scanner_source, external_id)
logAction(webhook.aikido.received, { count })
200 { received: true, count }

outputs: New rows (or no-op upserts) in findings table
Audit log entry per webhook batch
failureModes: Invalid HMAC → 401
Org header missing → falls back to 'default' org id
Adapter normalization gap → finding silently shaped with low confidence

flows.name: Repository Indexing (RAG)
flows.summary: On demand or per repo connect, the indexer clones the repo, splits sources by function/line boundary, embeds chunks with Voyage's voyage-code-3, and upserts them into a Pinecone namespace shaped {orgId}/{repo}/{branch}. The validated-fix pipeline later queries this namespace for context chunks.
flows.trigger: POST /api/repositories/:repo/index from dashboard, or reconnect flow

steps.action: POST /api/repositories/:repo/index
enqueueIndexJob({ repo, branch, orgId, githubToken })
Pulls job from index-queue
Fetch source tree / tarball via Octokit
Filter to .ts/.tsx/.js/.py/.go/.java/.rs/.rb; skip node_modules, dist, lockfiles
Chunk by function/class boundaries, fallback ~100-line windows with overlap
Batch-embed chunks (voyage-code-3, up to 128/call)
upsertVectors(namespace={orgId}/{repo}/{branch}, vectors)
upsert codebase_indices row + audit log

outputs: Pinecone namespace populated with embeddings + metadata
codebase_indices row with chunk count + last-indexed timestamp
failureModes: Voyage rate limit → batch retries
Pinecone quota → partial upsert, namespace left in mixed state
Repo too large → chunk explosion; mitigated by file-type filter

flows.name: On-Demand Finding Analysis
flows.summary: From a finding detail page the user can run a one-shot analysis pass. The dashboard calls Claude with the finding + repo context and returns a markdown report (Recommended Fix, Proposed Diff). The report is later prepended to the fix prompt as 'Prior Analysis'.
flows.trigger: User clicks 'Analyze' on a finding detail page

steps.action: POST /api/findings/analyze with findingId
Query top-k chunks for the affected file/symbol
Fetch raw vulnerable file via Octokit
Run analysis prompt (Claude) — split input/output cached for cost UI
Stream markdown report back to the finding page

outputs: Markdown analysis stored with the finding (used as priorAnalysis on next fix trigger)
Token-usage row recorded for analysis pricing
failureModes: Pinecone namespace missing → analysis runs without RAG context
Anthropic key invalid → 401, surfaced in UI
Repo not indexed → user prompted to index first

flows.name: User Triggers a Validated Fix
flows.summary: The dashboard proxies the trigger request to the backend, attaching the user's Aikido and Anthropic credentials from encrypted cookies plus the latest prior-analysis markdown. The backend resolves a service JWT, mints a short-lived GitHub installation token, and enqueues a validation job.
flows.trigger: User clicks 'Generate Fix' on a finding (or 'Retry' on a failed attempt)

steps.action: POST /api/findings/[id]/validated-fix/trigger { targetBranch?, reviewers?, maxAttempts?, priorAnalysis? }
Decrypt aikido_connection + anthropic_connection cookies
POST /api/findings/:id/validated-fix with credentials in body + service JWT
Load finding, organization, custom prompts
validationQueue.add({ findingId, orgId, aikidoApiKey, anthropicApiKey, priorAnalysis, ... })
202 { jobId, attemptId }

outputs: findings.status set to 'fixing' by the worker on dequeue
failureModes: Kill switch enabled → 'validated_fix.killed' audit entry, no job enqueued
Org has no GitHub App install → job still enqueued; pipeline will fail at PR step
Aikido/Anthropic cookies missing → pipeline falls back to env keys or OSS scanners

flows.name: Validated-Fix Pipeline (one attempt)
flows.summary: The validation worker drives a sandboxed loop per finding: fetch repo tarball, then for each attempt extract a fresh workspace, run the agentic generator (Claude + tool-use against the sandbox), apply the patch, generate tests, install, run tests, re-scan, open the PR, and wait for CI. Each stage failure is recorded; on retry the next iteration sees the failure output as feedback.
flows.trigger: Validation worker pulls a job from validation-queue

steps.action: Load finding + org; update finding.status = 'fixing'
Mint installation token via GitHub App JWT
triage(finding) — skip if not auto-fixable
fetchRepoTarball(repo, branch, token) — resolves default branch when none given
createWorkspace(tarball) — fresh extraction per attempt
steps.detail: Prevents prior rejected patch from poisoning next git apply

steps.action: Insert fix_attempts row (status='running', attempt_number, parent_attempt_id)
generateFixAgentic — Claude with sandbox tool-use, prior analysis prepended, prior-failure feedback appended
applyPatch(workspace, diff) — record patch sandbox-log
runTestGenerationAgent — Claude proposes test file(s) targeting the fix
install() — run package manager install in the sandbox
runTests(paths) — execute generated tests
runSecurityScan(finding, workspace) — Aikido or OSS fallback; verdict ∈ resolved | still-vulnerable | inconclusive
Persist validation status BEFORE PR step (so UI shows 'validated' even if PR fails)
submitMultiFile — create branch sutura/fix-{findingId}, write fix + test files, open PR
awaitCiVerdict — poll check_runs on PR head SHA up to ciTimeoutMs (default 10 min)
Update fix_attempts with ci_check_status + ci_failure_logs; mark succeeded / failed / exhausted
logAction(validated_fix.opened | validated_fix.failed)

outputs: fix_attempts row per attempt with diff, test files, sandbox logs, scan output, PR URL, CI verdict
Successful attempt → finding.status='fixed', PR open on GitHub
failureModes: Patch rejected → next attempt restarts from clean tarball with the reject text in feedback
Install / test failure → recorded; retry uses tail of stdout+stderr as feedback
Rescan still vulnerable → attempt failed even though tests passed
CI failure → ci_failure_logs (head+tail, ≤64KB) become next iteration's feedback
Sandbox image missing → fail-fast with operator-actionable warning
Kill switch ON → pipeline aborts with reason='kill_switch' before any work

flows.name: Agentic Fix Loop (retry feedback)
flows.summary: When an attempt fails at any stage — patch, install, tests, rescan, or CI — the next iteration of the pipeline starts from a clean workspace but feeds the prior failure stage + output back into the prompt. The generator runs as a tool-using Claude agent so it can read the sandbox before re-emitting the diff.
flows.trigger: Previous attempt set lastFailure; attempt counter < maxAttempts (default 3)

steps.action: lastFailure = { stage, output (tail 4-16KB) } captured from prior attempt
Fresh workspace extraction from same tarball
Prompt prepend: Prior Analysis (cap 12KB tail); append: 'Previous attempt #N failed at stage X' + output tail
Tool calls: read files, run probes, list directories — agent inspects current state
Emit corrected unified diff (+ optional reasoning)
Loop back into patch → tests → scan → PR → CI

outputs: Chained fix_attempts rows linked by parent_attempt_id
On exhaustion, last row marked status='exhausted'; finding.status='failed'
failureModes: Generator emits no diff → recorded as 'no_diff', counts as one attempt
Agent loops without convergence → maxAttempts is the hard ceiling
Lock duration is 45 min so CI polling (≤10 min × 3 attempts) fits in one worker lock

flows.name: Dashboard Read Paths
flows.summary: All read pages — overview, findings, fix history, repositories, audit log, settings, prompts, analytics, token costs — fetch from the backend via the dashboard's backend-client wrapper. A service-token JWT is generated per request from the configured DEFAULT_ORG_ID.
flows.trigger: User navigates to any dashboard page

steps.action: Open page (e.g. /findings, /fixes, /audit-log)
GET /api/findings | /api/fixes | /api/audit-log | /api/org | /api/repositories with Authorization: Bearer <service-jwt>
Supabase query with org_id filter (RLS bypass via service key)
Paginated JSON { data, total, page, pageSize }
Render cards/tables with loading + error states

outputs: Token-costs page joins token_usage rows by operation (analysis vs fix_generation) for split cost UI
failureModes: Backend unreachable → page shows offline state
DEFAULT_ORG_ID misconfigured → 'org not found' on every page

flows.name: Audit Logging
flows.summary: Every mutating action — webhook receipt, fix trigger, fix outcome, settings change — writes a row to audit_log with actor, action, resource type/id, and structured metadata. The dashboard's /audit-log page renders this in reverse-chronological order with search.
flows.trigger: Any mutating call across backend or workers

steps.action: logAction({ org_id, actor, action, resource_type, resource_id?, metadata_json })
logAction(validated_fix.opened | validated_fix.failed | validated_fix.killed)
Webhook receipt logs include batch counts

outputs: Append-only audit_log rows surfaced in /audit-log UI
failureModes: Audit insert errors are swallowed with .catch(() => {}) so failures don't block primary actions
